free_tier.stated: No quota — media is retained indefinitely. The docs say Twilio 'retains the stored media until you delete the related Media subresource instance', i.e. retention is customer-controlled and unbounded in time.

retention.stated: No quota — media is retained indefinitely

egress.terms: Authenticated only, and Twilio says so outright: 'If you need to embed media in web applications without exposing your credentials, download the media files and serve them from your own server or cloud storage service.' No public URL, ever.

tooling: twilio-python / twilio-node; .media.list() and .media(sid).fetch(). Clean API, but nothing removes the auth requirement.
chaining: 5 MB per message is the wall. To reach 1 TB you need ~200,000 MMS, each billed per message — this is the opposite of a free tier. Retention is excellent and completely unusable at this scale.
limits_note: 5 MB TOTAL across up to 10 files per message; 'Twilio rejects messages with over 5MB of media'. Paid per message ($ per MMS segment), not a free tier. Carrier-grade resizing mangles images.
reliability_note: The best retention semantics in the slot (never expires unless you delete) ruined by a 5 MB message cap and per-message billing. Interesting only as proof that indefinite retention is commercially possible.

evidence.proved: read live: 'Twilio retains the stored media until you delete the related Media subresource instance.'
read live: 'up to 10 media files that have a total size of up to 5MB ... Twilio rejects messages with over 5MB of media'
